memory_update.text: MKSI should be tracked as a US-listed underfollowed substrate/process-chemistry candidate because Atotech maps directly to package substrate copper processes, plating, via filling, and advanced packaging process control.
CAMT should be tracked as a yield-inspection beneficiary of HBM/chiplet/advanced-packaging complexity, especially if order disclosures continue to reference tier-1 OSATs and HBM manufacturers.

PDFS is a lower-attention software/data platform hypothesis for advanced-packaging yield orchestration; survival in later layers requires customer-specific evidence tied to OSAT, packaging, or HBM/chiplet workflows.

AMKR is best used as a reference demand/customer anchor for this node, not as the underfollowed alpha lane, because it is a visible OSAT advanced-packaging provider rather than a hidden substrate/material supplier.

Most direct ABF substrate and insulating-film leaders are not clean US-listed common stocks; next pass should separately map OTC/foreign listings such as Ajinomoto, Ibiden, Unimicron, Shinko, Kinsus, AT&S, and MEC if the mandate allows non-US primary listings.

node: Advanced packaging substrates, ABF-style insulating materials, and copper-bonding chemistry
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the substrate/material/yield layer below AI accelerators and HBM. Because the most direct ABF substrate and specialty film leaders are mostly non-US-listed or OTC/non-primary listings, the strongest US-listed mapping is second-order: OSAT advanced packaging capacity, substrate/process-chemistry suppliers, inspection/metrology, and yield-data platforms. The underfollowed lane is led by MKSI, CAMT, and PDFS; AMKR is included as a reference anchor because it is a direct advanced-packaging service provider and potential beneficiary/customer of substrate and bonding-material constraints.
